chains.title: Null: no allele-specific TF-mediated effect at C250T; recurrent somatic TERT promoter hotspot or linked causal variant.
predictions: No reproducible allele-specific TF binding difference between ref G and alt A at C250T
No allele-specific effect on TERT expression attributable to this variant
Disease association is explained by the recurrent somatic TERT promoter hotspot or a linked causal variant, not by a TF-mediated allelic effect
falsified_if: Robust allele-specific TF binding at C250T is demonstrated and perturbing that TF changes TERT expression in the relevant cell context
The disease association is shown to be caused by this allele acting through a TF rather than by the recurrent somatic hotspot or a linked causal variant

chains.title: C250T is proposed to strengthen a GABPA-bound ETS site and increase TERT in glioblastoma.

links.claim: GABPA is nominated as the ETS-family TF, and the alt A allele is predicted to bind GABPA more strongly. E05 shows GABPA ChIP peaks containing the variant in HepG2 and SK-N-SH, but no GABPA peak in glioblastoma and no allele-specific binding test. QBiC-SELEX coverage for GABPA is not_checked because no screen row or qbic_tf_detail lookup was supplied.
The variant lies in the TERT promoter ENSR5_832QG and in promoter-like cCRE EH38E3622530, so a putative ETS-site change would act in a TERT promoter element.
TERT is the nearest protein-coding gene, 0.0 kb from its TSS upstream on the minus-strand gene; CLPTM1L is 50 kb away.

The relevant cell type is glioblastoma per the case context, but E03 gives maxima over ENCODE biosamples rather than glioblastoma-specific activity, and E05 provides no glioblastoma GABPA peak; glioblastoma-specific GABPA occupancy is therefore unproven.

TERT activation is a plausible oncogenic mechanism in glioblastoma, and E04 contains general TERT-glioblastoma literature, but no C250T-specific or GABPA-specific TERT activation evidence is supplied.

predictions: Allele-specific GABPA ChIP-qPCR, EMSA or reporter assays show alt A > ref G at C250T in glioblastoma cells
GABPA knockdown or knockout reduces TERT expression in glioblastoma cells carrying the alt allele
Disrupting the predicted ETS motif abolishes the allele-specific effect
falsified_if: No allele-specific GABPA binding is detectable at C250T in a relevant cellular context
GABPA perturbation does not change TERT expression in cells carrying the alt allele
Mutating the predicted ETS motif does not abolish any allele-specific effect

chains.title: C250T is proposed to weaken CTCF binding at the TERT promoter cCRE, altering promoter architecture and TERT expression.

links.claim: CTCF is nominated as the architectural TF, and the ref G allele is predicted to bind CTCF more strongly than alt A. E03 gives only a maximum CTCF z-score of 2.0 in the containing cCRE, and E07 reports no CTCF peak containing the variant in glioblastoma but 2 CTCF peaks containing it in DOHH2 and endodermal cells; neither test is allele-specific. QBiC-SELEX coverage for CTCF is not_checked because no screen row or qbic_tf_detail lookup was supplied.
The variant lies in promoter-like cCRE EH38E3622530 and the TERT promoter ENSR5_832QG, so a CTCF change would affect a TERT promoter/architectural element.
TERT is the nearest protein-coding gene at 0.0 kb from its TSS, and E01 annotates the variant as upstream of TERT.

The supplied context is glioblastoma, but E03 lacks glioblastoma-specific CTCF occupancy or cCRE activity, and E07 provides no glioblastoma CTCF peak; glioblastoma-specific CTCF action is therefore unproven.

Altered TERT promoter architecture could change TERT expression and contribute to glioblastoma, but E04 links TERT to glioblastoma only generally and does not establish a CTCF-dependent mechanism or the direction of TERT expression change.

predictions: Allele-specific CTCF ChIP shows ref G > alt A at C250T in glioblastoma cells
The alt allele changes promoter contact or insulation in glioblastoma cells
CTCF depletion alters TERT expression or promoter architecture in the presence of the ref allele
falsified_if: No allele-specific CTCF binding difference is detected at C250T
CTCF perturbation does not alter TERT promoter architecture or TERT expression
The ref allele does not preserve a functional CTCF site better than the alt allele

chains.title: C250T is proposed to strengthen an ETS1-bound ETS site and increase TERT in melanoma or bladder cancer.

links.claim: ETS1 is an alternative ETS-family TF, and the alt A allele is predicted to bind ETS1 more strongly. E06 reports no ETS1 ChIP peak containing the variant in melanoma and no peak within 100 bp without containing it, so ETS1 occupancy at this element is unsupported. QBiC-SELEX coverage for ETS1 is not_checked because no screen row or qbic_tf_detail lookup was supplied.
The variant is in the TERT promoter ENSR5_832QG and promoter-like cCRE EH38E3622530, placing any ETS1 effect at a TERT promoter element.
TERT is the nearest protein-coding gene at 0.0 kb from its TSS; E01 annotates the variant as upstream of TERT.

Melanoma and bladder cancer are in the case header, but E04 contains only general TERT/melanoma literature with no bladder-specific top hit, and E06 provides no melanoma ETS1 occupancy; cell-type-specific ETS1 action is not established.
TERT activation is linked generally to melanoma in E04, but there is no C250T- or ETS1-specific TERT activation evidence in melanoma or bladder cancer.

predictions: ETS1 binds the alt allele more strongly than ref at C250T in melanoma or bladder assays
ETS1 knockdown reduces TERT expression in cells carrying the alt allele
The effect is weaker or absent in glioblastoma compared with a GABPA-dependent effect
falsified_if: ETS1 does not bind the alt allele more strongly than ref in melanoma or bladder assays
ETS1 perturbation does not alter TERT expression in cells carrying the alt allele
The variant shows no ETS1-dependent allele-specific effect in the relevant disease context

grades_v0.reason: No evidence ID is cited for GABPA binding; the claim itself states direct allele-specific binding is not shown. GABPA is an ETS-family candidate without QBiC-SELEX coverage or motif/perturbation evidence, so the binding link is unsupported.
E01 places the variant in TERT promoter ENSR5_832QG, and E03 places it in promoter-like cCRE EH38E3622530 (PLS). This directly supports a TERT promoter element location.
E02 reports TERT at 0.0 kb from its TSS upstream, the nearest protein-coding gene; E01 reports TERT upstream_gene_variant. CLPTM1L is 50 kb away.

The case context is glioblastoma, but E03 gives only maxima across ENCODE biosamples, not glioblastoma-specific cCRE activity, and no GABPA occupancy in glioblastoma is shown. Glioblastoma specificity is therefore indirect.
E04 provides general TERT-cancer literature hits, including glioblastoma-related titles, but no C250T-specific TERT activation evidence. The phenotype link is plausible but indirect.
No evidence ID is cited for ETS1 binding; ETS1 is proposed only as an alternative ETS-family TF. No allele-specific binding, motif, or QBiC-SELEX evidence is supplied.
E01 and E03 directly place the variant in TERT promoter ENSR5_832QG and promoter-like cCRE EH38E3622530, supporting a TERT promoter element location.
E02 identifies TERT as the nearest gene at 0.0 kb from its TSS; E01 annotates the variant as upstream of TERT.

Melanoma and bladder are in the case header, and E04 has general melanoma/TERT hits, but no ETS1 occupancy or cCRE activity is shown in melanoma or bladder, and bladder is not represented in the top E04 titles.
E04 contains general TERT/melanoma literature, but no C250T- or ETS1-specific TERT activation evidence in melanoma or bladder. The link is indirect.

E03 shows only a modest CTCF z-score of 2.0 in the containing cCRE, as a maximum over biosamples. It does not test CTCF binding at the variant or allele-specific CTCF binding, so this is at best indirect.
E01 and E03 directly locate the variant in TERT promoter ENSR5_832QG and PLS cCRE EH38E3622530, supporting a promoter/architectural element location.
E02 reports TERT as the nearest protein-coding gene at 0.0 kb from its TSS; E01 reports it as upstream of TERT.
The supplied context is glioblastoma, but E03 lacks glioblastoma-specific CTCF occupancy or cCRE activity. No cell-type-specific CTCF evidence is provided.

E04 links TERT to glioblastoma generally, but not to a CTCF-dependent mechanism. The direction of the effect on TERT is also unspecified: ref G is proposed to bind CTCF more, but the consequence for TERT expression is not stated.

grades_final.reason: E05 shows GABPA ChIP peaks containing the variant only in HepG2/SK-N-SH, not glioblastoma, and gives no allele-specific binding test; it is consistent with GABPA occupancy at the element in some contexts but does not establish alt>A binding. QBiC-SELEX coverage is not_checked; a screen/qbic_tf_detail lookup for GABPA is needed.
E01 places the variant in promoter ENSR5_832QG and E03 places it in promoter-like cCRE EH38E3622530, directly supporting a TERT promoter element location.
E02 and E01 directly annotate TERT as the nearest protein-coding gene at 0.0 kb upstream; this supports the gene assignment, though it is proximity/annotation rather than functional regulation.
E03 reports maxima over ENCODE biosamples, not glioblastoma-specific cCRE activity, and E05 reports no glioblastoma GABPA peak; glioblastoma-specific GABPA action at this element is unsupported.
E04 provides general TERT-glioblastoma literature, consistent with a TERT oncogenic role, but no C250T-specific or GABPA-specific evidence linking this allele to glioblastoma phenotype.

checks.why: Tests whether GABPA occupies the variant-containing TERT promoter in the relevant glioblastoma context; a peak would upgrade the currently missing binding link, while absence would weaken H1.
Tests ETS1 occupancy at this promoter in a melanoma context; this is the key missing evidence for the alternative ETS1 chain.
Tests whether CTCF actually occupies the variant-containing cCRE in glioblastoma, which the current cCRE signal alone does not establish.

next_experiment: Allele-specific GABPA ChIP-qPCR at C250T in heterozygous glioblastoma cells is the cheapest experiment that separates H0 from H1: H1 predicts alt A > ref G GABPA binding, whereas H0 predicts no reproducible allelic difference.
